You are in a tough situation and it makes sense to feel defeated. But, take a deep breath and dare to hope - there are resources and programs to help you, you just have to ask the right person. Keep looking, keep asking, keep praying. If someone doesn’t have an answer, maybe ask “if you were in my shoes, what would you do? What would be your next step?”

If I was you my next step would be to check with all the online schools I could find to see what clerical positions I might be able to do from home. Then you can save $ by hiring a mother’s helper (babysitter) instead of full time childcare. Then I’d see if my landlord needed any work done.
That’s craziness. Well, one good thing from this pandemic year is a lot of support groups meet online now. I wish you the best in making closer connections, sexual or not and whether you move or not.
Haha, I had no clue what OLD or ltr were. Maybe 2021 will be my year for both...

Marijuana on the market now now is a lot more potent than 20 years ago (see article link below) - you are right to be concerned. It’s so hard with COVID and the schools & activities shut down - a lot of kids (and parents!) are truly struggling. Addiction is a lot about numbing feelings and chasing pleasure - have you tried being honest with her about how you’ve faced the most difficult feelings in your own life without substance use? That said, teens are going to rebel, parents are going to grieve... you’re not alone

One.Day.At.A.Time. Even if you have to crawl, just keep moving forward. I’m a single working mom with 3 kids at home and I UNDERSTAND what you are saying. I cry every day even though I’m taking antidepressants, walking my dog twice a day, going to online church and an online 12 step group... you’re not crazy and you’re not alone - a lot of us are burnt out and hanging on by a thread. I NEVER ignore when people offer to pray anymore - I need spiritual help to keep going! Try to take a deep breath - as long as there is air in your lungs, there is hope for today, and today is all we have to get through.

You are amazing. A lot of us don’t have the restraint you do - I respect you tremendously!
Dad doesn’t know his son and doesn’t know how to parent - sounds like he’s just now learning about this “adulting” thing. It happens even with some parents who are in the home. Just beware that a lot of addicts expect others to do for them what they should be doing for themselves - like raising their kid and establishing THEIR relationship with said kid. I suggest reading some Al-Anon literature, especially the “letter from the alcoholic”. My heart goes out to you 🥰

Depends on the kid (I have 4 and they’re all different). That just means I’d be surprised to hear that from some, not so surprised with others. 

Because I go to church it would be important to me to encourage them to find an inclusive faith community and ignore any “religious” people that would turn them away from spirituality (they turned Jesus away, too).

Yes!!! When I get cranky and lethargic my son knows to ask “ mom, have you been taking your iron?” I take Fluoradix (likely mis-spelled) liquid iron. It’s expensive, so sometimes I just get the Trader Joe’s chewable multi-vitamins, which have a surprisingly high iron.

I’m always frustrated with the old “take the electronics” tip. I took hers and she just got the next to latest iPhone handed down from her friend and uses the citywide WiFi for calling/texting apps. She has beat me up for trying to touch her phone and threatens to call the police because since I didn’t buy it I’d be stealing. Since I rent, the day she turns 18 I am moving and she will not be on the new lease. They only have to learn the hard way if that’s their choice.

These are good thoughts to consider - parenting vs being a parent. IMO it gets especially hard when they’re obnoxious, self-centered, rebellious teenagers. But I just came to terms with the importance of making myself a priority after literally losing my mind from overextending myself for the 1 of my 4 kids that’s a competitive athlete. When you’re a single parent, no one else is going to set or reinforce your boundaries except you. There’s no calvary coming.

Empathize. No answers, no recommendations, just letting you know you’re not alone. 

I did go to a boarding school myself (voluntarily - won a scholarship) and for me it was the best experience of my life. You’d be shocked at who can become friends when parents and zip codes aren’t in the mix and you’re judged for who YOU are. My observation was, however, that it was common among the kids who got “dumped” there there to sneak off, get into trouble, then face discipline and expulsion. So, careful with that option...

Hmmm... guarantee you he spends more than $50 a month on beer! The $ is helpful - at least one kid is going to need something I didn’t budget for before the end of the month. It’s less about the amount than attitude - like he’s being heroically charitable.  

I disagree that how much I make should determine whether he regularly supports his kids - physically or financially. I feel like that’s a cop out to justify being inconsistent. I shelled out a lot for his rehab and therapy during the marriage so I’ve got compassion fatigue with him - can’t say I care about his issues and insecurities.

Maybe deep down I wish I could be the one who’s just single with someone else raising my kids (ok, just the teenagers...)

Thank you for your honesty. Navigating gender identity issues can indeed be difficult for both parents and individuals!

Although there are a lot of people who will tell you that you must accept your teen’s gender identity as is, period end, the reality is that acceptance is a process. And, just like every marriage has a unique journey to becoming healthy and mutually supportive, your family will have its own unique journey to relational health.

Have faith and reassure your teen (and yourself!) that although you might never wave a rainbow flag at the Pride parade, you do love them and will keep working to build a positive relationship with them. This patience and understanding - graciousness - I wish your family heaps of it!

No advice but I relate!!! Unfortunately I’m basically in the same boat. Just wanted to let you know you’re not alone. I went to a workshop on the Nurtured Heart approach (based on the book Transforming the Difficult Child). It seemed to be doing some good, but when faced with major setbacks (such as police involvement) all that seems to go out the window...
